# CRW-1028: the triggers of the pre-merge evaluation crw1028-7b713d91 (head 7b713d910, defects d1 to d18), as the evaluation spells them,
# judged by the three gates on the final head. A trigger the reader now reads as an unknown program (field splitting, an env-run cd, parallel,
# a git driver command) is refused in every gate (U); the evaluation's R verdict is the worktree guard's deny, which U includes.
# Format: see shellwrite_repro_test.go.

=== CRW-1028-ev-d1-block | W
--why d1: a brace group's redirection creates a protected memory file.
{ :; } > {MEMORY}/n.md

=== CRW-1028-ev-d1-subshell | W
--why d1: a subshell's redirection.
( : ) > {MEMORY}/n.md

=== CRW-1028-ev-d1-if | W
--why d1 variant: an if compound's redirection.
if :; then :; fi > {MEMORY}/n.md

=== CRW-1028-ev-d1-while | W
--why d1 variant: a loop compound's redirection.
while false; do :; done > {MEMORY}/n.md

=== CRW-1028-ev-d2-cd-unknown-abs | R
--why d2: after a cd .. the cwd is known (slot root), the absolute checkout path is still refused.
cd ..; rm -rf {CHECKOUT}

=== CRW-1028-ev-d2-cd-var-abs | R
--why d2 variant: an unknown cwd (cd to a variable) and the absolute checkout path.
cd "$X"; rm -rf {CHECKOUT}

=== CRW-1028-ev-d2-cd-sub-abs | R
--why d2 variant: unknown cwd by a command substitution.
cd $(pwd)/..; rm -rf {CHECKOUT}

=== CRW-1028-ev-d3-split | U
--why d3: an unquoted variable holding several words is field-split into rm.
bash -c 'CMD="rm -rf ../repo"; $CMD'

=== CRW-1028-ev-d3-split-top | U
--why d3 variant: the same at the top level.
CMD="rm -rf ../repo"; $CMD

=== CRW-1028-ev-d4-env-cd | U
--why d4: env runs cd in a child, the caller cwd stays.
env cd /tmp; rm -rf ../repo

=== CRW-1028-ev-d4-nohup-func | R
--why d4 variant: a function called through nice.
f() { cd /tmp; }; nice f; rm -rf ../repo

=== CRW-1028-ev-d5-while-false | R
--why d5: a loop that runs zero times.
while false; do cd /tmp; done; rm -rf ../repo

=== CRW-1028-ev-d5-for | R
--why d5 variant: a for loop with an empty list.
for i in; do cd /tmp; done; rm -rf ../repo

=== CRW-1028-ev-d6-parallel | U
--why d6: parallel's ::: input is the removal target.
parallel rm -rf {} ::: {CHECKOUT}

=== CRW-1028-ev-d7-cd-memory | W
--why d7: cd into the memory root, relative write.
--file {MEMORY}/seed.md
x
--cmd
cd {MEMORY}; echo x > n.md

=== CRW-1028-ev-d7-func-cd | W
--why d7 variant: a function that cds.
--file {MEMORY}/seed.md
x
--cmd
f() { cd {MEMORY}; }; f; echo x > n.md

=== CRW-1028-ev-d8-find-delete | R
--why d8: find -depth -delete in the checkout.
find . -depth -delete

=== CRW-1028-ev-d8-find-delete-abs | R
--why d8 variant: find -delete on the absolute checkout.
find {CHECKOUT} -delete

=== CRW-1028-ev-d8-python-rmtree | R
--why d8: python shutil.rmtree of the checkout.
python3 -c 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("{CHECKOUT}")'

=== CRW-1028-ev-d9-json-secret | P
--why d9: a JSON body with a credential assignment.
--file {TMP}/post.json
{"body":"MY_API_KEY=sentinel"}
--cmd
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments -X POST --input {TMP}/post.json

=== CRW-1028-ev-d9-json-escaped | P
--why d9 variant: the assignment spelled with a JSON escape (\u003d is =); the file text has no NAME=value, only the decoded string does.
--file {TMP}/post2.json
{"body":"MY_API_KEY\u003dsentinel"}
--cmd
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments -X POST --input {TMP}/post2.json

=== CRW-1028-ev-d9-json-escaped-name | P
--why d9 variant: a letter of the name escaped as well (\u004b is K) next to the escaped =.
--file {TMP}/post3.json
{"body":"MY_API_\u004bEY\u003dsentinel"}
--cmd
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments -X POST --input {TMP}/post3.json

=== CRW-1028-ev-d10-double-coding | E
--why d10: a second coding declaration in a bytes exec program.
python3 -c 'exec(br"""# coding note; coding: unicode_escape
\x6fpen(file="{MEMORY}/n.md",mode="w")
""")'

=== CRW-1028-ev-d11-node-argv | W
--why d11: node writeFileSync with argv destination.
node -e 'require("fs").writeFileSync(process.argv[1],"x")' {MEMORY}/n.md

=== CRW-1028-ev-d11-python-f-open | W
--why d11: python open function value alias.
python3 -c 'm="{MEMORY}/n.md"; f=open; f(m,"w").write("x")'

=== CRW-1028-ev-d11-python-path-computed | W
--why d11 control: a computed Path whose protected root stays a literal in the text is a write attempt on the evaluated head 7b713d910 as well; the shapes below are the ones that head missed.
python3 -c 'import pathlib; pathlib.Path("{MEMORY}/"+"n.md").write_text("x")'

=== CRW-1028-ev-d11-python-path-join | W
--why d11: a Path joined with joinpath; read as no write by 7b713d910 through e5c8f308f, fixed by 87ba17721.
python3 -c 'import pathlib; pathlib.Path("{MEMORY}").joinpath("n.md").write_text("x")'

=== CRW-1028-ev-d11-python-path-div | W
--why d11: a Path built with the / operator; read as no write by 7b713d910 through e5c8f308f, fixed by 87ba17721.
python3 -c 'import pathlib; (pathlib.Path("{MEMORY}")/"n.md").write_text("x")'

=== CRW-1028-ev-d11-python-path-bound | W
--why d11: a Path bound to a name and written through the name; read as no write by 7b713d910 through e5c8f308f, fixed by 87ba17721.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; p=Path("{MEMORY}/n.md"); p.write_text("x")'

=== CRW-1028-ev-d12-ruby | W
--why d12: ruby File.write.
ruby -e 'File.write("{MEMORY}/n.md","x")'

=== CRW-1028-ev-d12-perl | W
--why d12: perl open for writing.
perl -e 'open(F,">","{MEMORY}/n.md"); print F "x"'

=== CRW-1028-ev-d12-sed-e | W
--why d12: sed e command runs a shell.
sed 'e echo x > {MEMORY}/n.md' <<<x

=== CRW-1028-ev-d13-input-dash | P

--file -
clean

gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments -X POST --input -

clean
--cmd

=== CRW-1028-ev-d14-link-outside | P
--why d14: a link in the temporary root to a file outside it.
--link {TMP}/body-link /etc/hostname
--cmd
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments --input {TMP}/body-link

=== CRW-1028-ev-d14-link-outside-body-file | P

--link {TMP}/body-link /etc/hostname
--cmd
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/body-link

=== CRW-1028-ev-d14-control-inside | B
--why d14 control: a link to a clean file inside the root.
--file {TMP}/real.json
{"body":"hello"}
--link {TMP}/inner-link {TMP}/real.json
--cmd
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments --input {TMP}/inner-link

=== CRW-1028-ev-d15-sort-output-eq | W
--why d15: sort --output=FILE.
sort --output={MEMORY}/n.md /tmp/input

=== CRW-1028-ev-d15-sort-o-joined | W
--why d15: sort -oFILE.
sort -o{MEMORY}/n.md /tmp/input

=== CRW-1028-ev-d15-sort-output-sep | W
--why d15: sort --output FILE.
sort --output {MEMORY}/n.md /tmp/input

=== CRW-1028-ev-d16-git-diff-command | U
--why d16: git -c diff.foo.command executes a program.
git -c 'diff.foo.command=sh -c "rm -rf {CHECKOUT}" --' diff --ext-diff

=== CRW-1028-ev-d17-fifo-bash | U
--why d17: a FIFO with no writer given to bash as a script.
--fifo {TMP}/fifo
--cmd
bash {TMP}/fifo

=== CRW-1028-ev-d17-fifo-body-file | P

=== CRW-1028-ev-d18-plain-string | B
--why d18: a plain string whose text is f'}' is no f-string.
python3 -c "print(\"f'}'\")"

=== CRW-1028-ev-overblock-01 | T
--why Control: at the top level the later script's rewrite of lint.sh reaches only the executions after it, so lint.sh is the file read (fix round 5).
--file lint.sh
echo lint
--file refresh.sh
echo refreshed > lint.sh
--cmd
bash lint.sh; bash refresh.sh

=== CRW-1028-ev-overblock-02 | T
--why Over-block, fixed by CRW-1059 (was a follow-up: sequential executions inside bash -c and command substitution see later scripts' writes): the same two scripts run in order inside bash -c, but a carried text is unordered for the body writes, so lint.sh counts as rewritten.
--file lint.sh
echo lint
--file refresh.sh
echo refreshed > lint.sh
--cmd
bash -c 'bash lint.sh; bash refresh.sh'

=== CRW-1028-ev-overblock-03 | T
--why Over-block, fixed by CRW-1059 (same follow-up): the same in a command substitution that runs after lint.sh.
--file lint.sh
echo lint
--file refresh.sh
echo refreshed > lint.sh
--cmd
bash lint.sh; x=$(bash refresh.sh)

=== CRW-1028-ev-overblock-04 | U
--why Control: the rewriting script first and the rewritten one after it is a real rewrite and is refused inside bash -c.
--file lint.sh
echo lint
--file refresh.sh
echo refreshed > lint.sh
--cmd
bash -c 'bash refresh.sh; bash lint.sh'
